requirements.text: A host turns the focus streak on per button with an optional boolean `focusSheen` field on the existing `zest` configuration object; it is off by default and works on a regular button and on a split button.
The focus streak plays when an opted-in button receives keyboard focus, not when it is clicked with a mouse, once per focus arrival; the existing focus ring stays the visible primary focus signal.

The streak is a diagonal light band at about 45 degrees that travels from the button's top-right area to its bottom-left across the whole button in about 0.6 seconds, is clipped to the button's rounded shape, and disappears when it finishes.
The streak is visible on all four button styles (solid, outline, text, dashed) and all three variants (standard, success, danger) in both light and dark themes, without making the label unreadable.

On a split button with the focus streak enabled, focusing either segment plays one sweep across the whole split control (main action and chevron together), clipped to the control's rounded outer corners; the open menu is not clipped, covered or hidden.
Turn the focus streak off for reduced motion. People who ask their device to reduce motion should not get a sweeping band.
Suppress the chevron mount streak when the focus streak is enabled. Two streaks on one split control would collide and look like a glitch.
Characterisation tests for the existing button appearance and chevron streak. The shared stylesheet is being edited, so the behaviour already shipped is pinned before the change.
Document the focus streak on every page readers use. A new prop that cannot be found is a feature nobody can use.

A host turns the focus streak on per button with an optional boolean `focusSheen` field on the existing `zest` configuration object; it is off by default and works on a regular button and on a split button.
tests: R1: focusSheen is off by default and opts in per button without leaking
R1: focusSheen={false} renders no streak layer
R1: turning focusSheen off at runtime removes the streak layer from a regular button and a split control
R1: a split button opts in with one whole-control layer and no per-segment layer
R1: opting in leaves the accessible name, role and pressed state alone

requirements.text: The focus streak plays when an opted-in button receives keyboard focus, not when it is clicked with a mouse, once per focus arrival; the existing focus ring stays the visible primary focus signal.
tests: R2: plain focus or a mouse click adds no JS state; only :focus-visible starts the sweep
R2: each focus arrival plays exactly one sweep and a re-focus replays it
R2: the existing focus ring remains the primary focus signal
R2: a toggle in its on state keeps its pressed look and focus ring while the streak plays

requirements.text: The streak is a diagonal light band at about 45 degrees that travels from the button's top-right area to its bottom-left across the whole button in about 0.6 seconds, is clipped to the button's rounded shape, and disappears when it finishes.
tests: R2: the existing focus ring remains the primary focus signal
R3: the band is a 45-degree diagonal that travels top-right to bottom-left over 0.6 seconds
R3: the band is clipped by the button's rounded overflow and never changes its layout
R3: the band ends transparent and is not left stuck or tinted
R3: very small and very large buttons share one continuous sweep with no stacked layers

requirements.text: The streak is visible on all four button styles (solid, outline, text, dashed) and all three variants (standard, success, danger) in both light and dark themes, without making the label unreadable.
tests: R4: every style, variant and forced theme gets the streak layer on a regular button
R4: every style, variant and forced theme gets the whole-control layer on a split button
R4: the band colour follows currentColor and the button's own theme tokens so it reads on every style
R4: the label sits above the translucent band so it stays readable

requirements.text: On a split button with the focus streak enabled, focusing either segment plays one sweep across the whole split control (main action and chevron together), clipped to the control's rounded outer corners; the open menu is not clipped, covered or hidden.
tests: R1: a split button opts in with one whole-control layer and no per-segment layer
R4: every style, variant and forced theme gets the whole-control layer on a split button
R5: a split control plays one whole-control sweep from either segment
R5: the split band is clipped to the rounded outer corners without clipping either focus ring
R5: the open menu is rendered outside the clipping wrapper and stays visible
R5: moving focus from the main segment to the chevron keeps one overlay for the whole visit

requirements.text: Turn the focus streak off for reduced motion. People who ask their device to reduce motion should not get a sweeping band.
tests: A1: reduced motion disables the focus streak for regular and split buttons
A1: without the preference the streak keeps its animation on both button kinds

requirements.text: Suppress the chevron mount streak when the focus streak is enabled. Two streaks on one split control would collide and look like a glitch.
tests: A2: an opted-in split control suppresses the chevron mount streak
A2: a split control that is not opted in keeps its chevron mount streak

requirements.text: Characterisation tests for the existing button appearance and chevron streak. The shared stylesheet is being edited, so the behaviour already shipped is pinned before the change.
tests: A3: a plain regular button keeps its current wrapper element, classes and DOM
A3: a split wrapper and its two segments keep their current classes and gain no sheen classes

A3: the existing chevron mount-streak rule and keyframes are unchanged
A3: a button that does not opt in keeps its click behaviour and adds no extra elements
